claude.sample_unit: cases (122,441 slides) in 3-year deployment; validation 101 cases/1279 slides

links.outcome: Local validation accuracy on Puerto Rican cohort vs original developer populations
links.effect: Cancer detection AUC 0.994 (95% CI 0.988-0.997), sensitivity 96.6%, specificity 96.7%, NPV 99.2%; Gleason GG1 vs GG2+ AUC 0.901, similar to original populations.
links.quote: Results show a similar high diagnostic accuracy for cancer in this Puerto Rican population as in the original populations vs benign with an AUC of 0.994 (95% CI: 0.988–0.997).

links.outcome: Pathologist review of AI alerts to resolve false-positive AI cancer calls
links.effect: In validation, all 17 false-positive slide alerts were resolved by pathologist review as benign mimics; in deployment, 1733 benign cases alerted but only 128 (2.9%) changed after review.
links.quote: Following pathologist review, all 17 slide alerts were resolved and shown to be triggered by glands (normal, atrophic, and seminal vesicle) as well as inflammation ( Table 2 ), features that may mimic malignant glands.

links.outcome: Pathologist-plus-AI second read vs pathologist alone diagnosis changes (AI Impact)
links.effect: 2.9% (128/4385) benign cases and 1.21% (24/1984) GG1 cases revised after AI alerts; overall AI Impact 1.8%, ranging 0.75% to 3.5% per pathologist.
links.quote: After review by the pathologist, 0.3% (155/57119) of the benign slides and 2.9% (128/4385) of benign cases required a change of diagnosis.

unlisted_practices: Using AI as a 100% quality-control second read applied to all slides after primary pathologist review, with alerts resolved before sign-out

openai.sample_unit: prostate biopsy cases analyzed during routine clinical deployment

links.outcome: False-negative cancer findings in slides labeled benign by AI
links.effect: AI called nine cancer slides benign; seven were GG1, and the other two were GG2 and GG4. No cancers were missed at the case level out of 1279 WSI.
links.quote: At the slide level, Galen™ called nine slides benign that were cancer.

links.outcome: Pathologist identification and resolution of false-positive AI cancer alerts
links.effect: Pathologist review resolved all 17 slide alerts across 12 validation cases as false positives triggered by benign tissue features.
links.quote: Following pathologist review, all 17 slide alerts were resolved and shown to be triggered by glands (normal, atrophic, and seminal vesicle) as well as inflammation ( Table 2 ), features that may mimic malignant glands.

links.outcome: Diagnostic revisions following AI-assisted second review in routine pathology workflow
links.effect: Over 3 years, diagnoses revised before sign-out yielded an overall AI Impact™ of 1.8%, ranging from 0.75% up to 3.5% per individual pathologist.
links.quote: In our real-world data, AI Impact™ ranged from 0.75% up to 3.5% per individual pathologist, with a normalized group effect of 1.8%.

links.outcome: cancer detection accuracy in local validation
links.effect: In the local validation set, the AI achieved an AUC of 0.994, with 96.6% sensitivity and 96.7% specificity.
links.quote: The AUC for cancer detection in the validation set was 0.994 (95% CI 0.988–0.997), with a 96.7% (95% CI 95.6–97.8) specificity and a 96.6% (95% CI 93.3–98.8) sensitivity.

links.outcome: false-negative rate reduction in clinical workflow
links.effect: Integrating the AI as a second-read system in the intended clinical workflow reduced the group's false-negative rate by 1.8%.
links.quote: The use of the Galen™ Prostate AI algorithm in a second-read implementation had the effect of providing alerts for review such that the false-negative rate of the group was reduced by the amount indicated by the AI Impact™.

links.outcome: rate of diagnosis change after AI alert
links.effect: During real-world deployment over 3 years, pathologists reviewed AI alerts and revised the diagnosis in 2.9% of benign cases.
links.quote: After review by the pathologist, 0.3% (155/57119) of the benign slides and 2.9% (128/4385) of benign cases required a change of diagnosis.

screen.practice: local validation before go-live and AI second-read use in routine pathology
screen.reason: Evaluates the validation and 3-year real-world clinical deployment of an AI second-read system in a CLIA-certified pathology laboratory.
